Model relationships and a marked date table
Author DAX for KPIs, targets, and toast alerts
Recreate the reference dashboard layout in Power BI Desktop

intentionalDifferences.detail: Students use corrected box-shadow syntax; reference PBIX measure omits a closing parenthesis.
DAX measure remains Total Orders (= SUM of Order qty). Students should title the card Units Sold; reference PBIX label says Total Orders.
Students use Csv.Document on packaged CSVs; author Excel M is reference-only.

stages.title: Import data
stages.summary: CSV imports with exact table names

steps.title: Know the target report
steps.objective: Recognize the finished executive sales page you will rebuild from a blank PBIX.
actions: Open the JobReady **Finished preview** (static PNG — interactions happen in Power BI Desktop).
Note canvas size 1280×780 and the KPI + trend + toast layout.
steps.expectedResult: You can describe where slicers, KPIs, bars, trend, settings, and toast sit on the page.
verificationChecklist: You understand this is a reference only

images.caption: Finished report canvas (reference).
images.alt: Executive sales dashboard with KPI cards, slicers, trend chart, and toast area

steps.title: Install tools
steps.objective: Use a Power BI Desktop build that supports HTML Content custom visuals.
actions: Install **Power BI Desktop** (tested with recent 2024–2025 builds).
From AppSource in Desktop, add custom visual **HTML Content** (package id htmlContent443BE3AD55E043BF878BED274D3A6855, version 1.2.1.17 in the reference file).
Create an empty folder for lab data, e.g. `C:\JobReady\executive-sales-data\`.
steps.expectedResult: Desktop opens, HTML Content visual is available in the visualizations pane.

steps.title: Download the student kit
steps.objective: Get CSVs and guides from JobReady.
actions: Download **All datasets (.zip)** and extract into your data folder.
Optional: download the reference `.pbix` only to compare — do not start from it for the graded rebuild.
verificationChecklist: data folder path has no spaces issues in M

steps.title: Create a blank report
steps.objective: Start from File → New to mirror the workshop path.
actions: File → New → Blank report.
Save as `Executive-Sales-Toast.pbix` in your lab folder.
steps.expectedResult: Empty report with one blank page.

steps.title: Create DataFolder parameter
steps.objective: One path drives all CSV imports.
actions: Home → Transform data → Manage Parameters → New.
Name: **DataFolder**, type Text, current value = folder containing the eight CSV files (trailing backslash optional).
verificationChecklist: Path opens without privacy errors on refresh

steps.title: Import Sales
steps.objective: Load `Sales.csv` as table **Sales** with explicit types.
actions: Home → Transform data → New Source → Blank Query.
Paste the M below (uses `DataFolder` parameter).
Rename query to **Sales** and ensure it loads to the model with table name **Sales**.
Close && Apply.

powerQuery.name: Sales
powerQuery.expression:
let
    Source = Csv.Document(
        File.Contents(DataFolder & "\Sales.csv"),
        [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]
    ),
    #"Promoted Headers" = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
    #"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Promoted Headers", {
            {"Sales Date", type date},
            {"Order qty", Int64.Type},
            {"unit price", type number},
            {"unit cost", type number},
            {"Productindex", Int64.Type},
            {"Storeindex", Int64.Type},
            {"Salesteamindex", Int64.Type},
            {"Sales_Index", Int64.Type},
            {"Order Number", type text},
            {"Sales Channel", type text}
        })
in
    #"Changed Type"

steps.expectedResult: Table **Sales** appears in the Fields pane.
steps.referenceNotes: Author Excel M is in power-query.json (reference only).

steps.title: Create D/W/M field parameter
steps.objective: Match the reference slicer that drives axis grain.
actions: Modeling → New parameter → Fields.
Add fields: Date Table[Date] (Day), Date Table[WeeknYear] (Week), Date Table[Month Short] (Month).
Name the parameter **Date M-W-D** (rename display column to `Date M-W-D` and order column `Date M-W-D Order`).
Do **not** import Date_M-W-D.csv expecting parameter metadata — that CSV is only a helper lookup.
steps.expectedResult: Slicer parameter with three values orders Day < Week < Month.
steps.referenceNotes: Reference binds charts to the field parameter, not bookmark-only grain switching.

steps.title: Hide helper columns
steps.objective: Reduce clutter.
actions: Hide technical columns on Date Table used only for sorting (Month Number, etc.) except those needed on visuals.
steps.expectedResult: Students can still sort months correctly.

steps.title: Measures: Total Sales, Average Daily Sales, Average Monthly Saeles…
steps.objective: Create DAX measures in dependency order.
actions: Modeling → New table → name it `# Measures` (hide later).
New measure for each formula below (home table `# Measures` unless noted).
Set format strings where specified in checklist.

dax.name: Total Sales
dax.expression:
Total Sales =
SUMX(
    Sales, 
    Sales[Order qty] * Sales[unit price] 
    )

dax.name: Average Daily Sales
dax.expression:
Average Daily Sales =
VAR _table = ALLSELECTED('Date Table')
VAR _Result = AVERAGEX( _table , [Total Sales] )
RETURN _Result

dax.name: Average Monthly Saeles
dax.expression:
Average Monthly Saeles =
VAR _table = VALUES('Date Table'[Month Short] )
VAR _Result = AVERAGEX( _table , [Total Sales] )
RETURN _Result

dax.name: Average Weekly Saeles
dax.expression:
Average Weekly Saeles =
VAR _table = VALUES( 'Date Table'[WeeknYear] )
VAR _Result = AVERAGEX( _table , [Total Sales] )
RETURN _Result

dax.name: Higher Percentile Value
dax.expression:
Higher Percentile Value =
SELECTEDVALUE('Higher Percentile'[Higher Percentile], 0.75)

dax.name: Higher Percentile of Dates
dax.expression:
Higher Percentile of Dates =
VAR _highPth = 'Higher Percentile'[Higher Percentile Value]
VAR _Result =
    SWITCH (
        TRUE (),
        ISINSCOPE ( 'Date Table'[Date] ), PERCENTILEX.EXC ( ALL( 'Date Table'[Date] ), [Total Sales], _highPth ),
        ISINSCOPE ( 'Date Table'[Month Short] ),
            PERCENTILEX.EXC (
                ALL( 'Date Table'[Month Short] ),
                [Total Sales],
                _highPth
            ),
        ISINSCOPE ( 'Date Table'[WeeknYear] ),
            PERCENTILEX.EXC (
                ALL( 'Date Table'[WeeknYear] ),
                [Total Sales],
                _highPth
            )
    )
RETURN
    _Result

dax.name: Color Formatting Line Chart
dax.expression:
Color Formatting Line Chart =
VAR _BottumColors = "#FA0C27" 
VAR _TopColors = "#1800ED"
VAR _MiddleColor = "#B6B1AF"
VAR _Result = 
SWITCH(
    TRUE(),
    [Total Sales] > [Higher Percentile of Dates], _TopColors,
    [Total Sales] < [Lower Percentile of Dates], _BottumColors,
    _MiddleColor
    )
RETURN _Result

dax.name: TS PM Current
dax.expression:
TS PM Current =
VAR _datetable =
 DATESINPERIOD( 
    'Date Table'[Date], MAX(Sales[Sales Date]), -1, MONTH )
VAR _result =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    _datetable
    )
RETURN _result

dax.name: TS PM Previous
dax.expression:
TS PM Previous =
VAR _datetable =
 DATESINPERIOD( 
    'Date Table'[Date], MAX(Sales[Sales Date]), -1, MONTH )
VAR _result =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    PREVIOUSMONTH(_datetable)
    )
RETURN _result

dax.name: TS MOM diff %
dax.expression:
TS MOM diff % =
DIVIDE(
    ([TS PM Current] - [TS PM Previous]),
    [TS PM Previous]
    )

Dashboard is filtered!   "&_Filter&" "&_Value&"

" )

Single product / store / team → singular label.

steps.title: Unfiltered KPI baseline
steps.objective: Match documented aggregates.
actions: Clear slicers.
Compare measures to `expected-results.json` → `displayCurrency` (2dp, reconciled profit).
verificationChecklist: Profit = Sales − Cost at display precision

steps.title: Save and reopen
steps.objective: Persistence check.
actions: Save PBIX, close Desktop, reopen and refresh.

formulas.Total Sales: SUM over rows of (Order qty × unit price) using Decimal per row
formulas.Total Cost: SUM over rows of (Order qty × unit cost) using Decimal per row
formulas.Total Profit: Total Sales − Total Cost at full precision (not a separate rolled-up import)
formulas.Profit Margin %: Total Profit / Total Sales at full precision

roundingPolicy.perRow: Decimal(str(qty)) * Decimal(str(price)) — avoids float drift in totals
roundingPolicy.displayCurrency: ROUND_HALF_UP to 2 decimal places for dollar KPI checks
roundingPolicy.displayProfit: money_round(Total Sales) − money_round(Total Cost) so cards reconcile
roundingPolicy.note: Do not compare rounded Sales minus a differently rounded Cost copied from prose; use this file.

expectedResults.notes: Verify in Power BI Desktop after model build; DAX SUMX may differ slightly in last digit vs Decimal CSV walk.
